requirement:
In authored chapters, requirements, examples, and named definitions render as
collapsible sections, expanded when the chapter opens. Body prose shares the
containing prose's left edge without added indentation. Each header's badge
is right-aligned and identifies the declaration and its kind.
A narrow colored bar in the right margin delineates the section and uses the
badge's color: blue for requirements and purple for examples. A square
disclosure control at the top of that bar shows a minus when expanded
and a plus when collapsed. Collapsing a section hides its body while keeping
the header visible. The disclosure works with a mouse or keyboard.

The body retains its Markdown rendering, including code blocks and nested
declarations. Requirement and example headers retain the definition and
evidence links described by {cite}`requirements.index.navigation`; those
links navigate independently of the disclosure.
rationale:
I found no test-adequacy gap for `requirements.index.declaration_sections`. The tests cover each obligation. - **Collapsible sections, expanded on open.** `declaration_sections_contain_their_headers_and_markdown_bodies` renders a requirement, a nested example and a definition. It asserts that exactly 3 `
` and `
` tags are balanced. - **Header and body structure.** The same test asserts that the header, which ends at ``, never contains `habeas-declaration-body`. Bodies sit in a separate `
`. Because the header stays outside the body, the header stays visible when the body is hidden. Hiding the body is native `
` behavior. - **Markdown bodies and nesting.** That test asserts rendered `` and `` text, a fenced `language-rust` code block, a nested declaration inside the requirement body, and the closing prose before `
`. It also asserts that surrounding prose is untouched and that the `:impl:` option line is removed. `colon_directives_render_markdown_bodies_and_legacy_roles_stay_literal` adds a check on `replace_definitions` that headings and code fences in the body survive. - **Definitions.** The same test asserts the definition header form, with `habeas-definition-label`, the phrase text and the escaped `&`, plus its Markdown body. - **Badge kind and name, and links in the header.** The same test checks both links for the requirement and the example. The kind link goes to `#habeas-{kind}-rules.{name}` with an `aria-label`. The name link goes to the evidence page. It also asserts that no `habeas-detail-icon` appears. Both links are inside the summary, so they work independently of the disclosure. - **Kind colors.** `declaration_badges_and_margin_controls_share_kind_colors` asserts `--habeas-declaration-color` is `#006ba8` for `req` and `#7151a1` for `example`. It also checks that the badge name is present and that there is no ` summary`. - **No added indentation.** `declaration_styles_distinguish_disclosure_state_and_keyboard_focus` asserts that `.habeas-declaration-body` has `padding: 0`. It also asserts a zero left margin and a right-only padding on `.habeas-declaration`. - **Margin bar and disclosure control.** The same test asserts the following. - The bar is a 3px right border. - `summary::after` is absolutely positioned at `top: 0; right: -13px`, with a border radius and the section color. - The control has a defined width, and the width equals the height, so it is square. - The collapsed state shows `content: "+"`. - `[open]` shows `content: "−"`. - **Keyboard use.** That test asserts a `:focus-visible::after` outline on the control. The summary is native, so Enter and Space toggle it. The visual rules are tested through the stylesheet's declarations, not through a browser. For this requirement that is adequate, because every stated visual property has an assertion tied to it. The assertions are correct against the requirement text. All the tests carry `{test}` references to the subject. I found no obligation left untested.

text: :::{req} declaration_sections
In authored chapters, requirements, examples, and named definitions render as
collapsible sections, expanded when the chapter opens. Body prose shares the
containing prose's left edge without added indentation. Each header's badge
is right-aligned and identifies the declaration and its kind.
A narrow colored bar in the right margin delineates the section and uses the
badge's color: blue for requirements and purple for examples. A square
disclosure control at the top of that bar shows a minus when expanded
and a plus when collapsed. Collapsing a section hides its body while keeping
the header visible. The disclosure works with a mouse or keyboard.
The body retains its Markdown rendering, including code blocks and nested
declarations. Requirement and example headers retain the definition and
evidence links described by {cite}`requirements.index.navigation`; those
links navigate independently of the disclosure.
:::{req} navigation
Each requirement and example declaration badge has two adjacent links. Its
kind (`req` or `example`) links to the declaration's anchor on the current
page; its full name links to the evidence detail page. These segments stay
together in one non-wrapping row, with no separate arrow link or plaintext evidence link.
Each detail page links back to the declaration's anchored badge and to the
index. Reference badges continue to link to the declaration. These links
resolve when a requirement name contains `.md`, as in
`requirements.cli.mdbook`.
